title: QUIC RFC 9000 STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED Frame Focused Proof
purpose: Describe the bounded RFC 9000 Section 19.13 STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED parser, formatter, field-boundary, and benchmark proof slice.
design_summary: The STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame remains centered on the existing span-backed frame codec and immutable frame view. The parser accepts the fixed STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame type 0x15, parses Stream ID and Maximum Stream Data as QUIC variable-length integers, preserves the blocked stream identifier and stream offset at which blocking occurred, and consumes exactly the STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame bytes so following packet frames remain available to the packet parser. The formatter writes the fixed type and both fields through the shared QUIC variable-length integer formatter and rejects values outside the 62-bit varint range.
data_and_state_considerations: This slice is wire-shape proof over QuicStreamDataBlockedFrame.StreamId, QuicStreamDataBlockedFrame.MaximumStreamData, and the frame codec. Runtime advisory emission remains owned by ARC-QUIC-RFC9000-0025. Receiver-side send-only stream rejection remains a separate requirement lane under RFC9000-S19-13-P2-R01.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Non-0x15 and non-minimal 0x15 frame-type encodings are rejected by the fixed-type parser.
Stream ID is accepted at each QUIC variable-length integer width boundary, including the maximum 62-bit varint value.
Maximum Stream Data is accepted at each QUIC variable-length integer width boundary, including the maximum 62-bit varint value.
Truncated Stream ID and Maximum Stream Data variable-length integers are rejected before a frame view is produced.
Formatter calls reject Stream ID and Maximum Stream Data values above the QUIC variable-length integer range.
The parser consumes only the STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame and leaves any trailing frame bytes for the packet parser.
alternatives_considered: Leave S19P13 under the existing broad frame-codec closeout; rejected because generated triage still reported broad or missing proof for requirements 0003 through 0008.
Fold receive-side send-only stream policy into this proof; rejected because RFC9000-S19-13-P2-R01 is a stream-state connection-error lane rather than parser and field-shape proof.

Create a standalone STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED benchmark suite; rejected because the existing QuicFrameCodec benchmark suite already owns permanent parser and formatter hot-path coverage for neighboring frame families.
risks: This proof does not claim new STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED emission scheduling or retry policy.
This proof does not close receiver-side send-only stream termination for RFC9000-S19-13-P2-R01.
Malformed-frame handling is proven at the codec seam, not as a hosted endpoint close-packet assertion for every malformed STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED input.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design covers RFC 9000 Section 19.13 STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED type encoding, Stream ID and Maximum Stream Data field varint encoding, field-boundary behavior, and parser/formatter benchmark coverage for requirements 0003 through 0008 only.
